messages:
elaine (Design): Pinging folks — quick design review request for the new Metrics dashboard chart. I uploaded a screenshot. Main asks: tick density on the x-axis feels cramped at desktop widths, unit abbreviations (ms vs milliseconds) are inconsistent, and one of the series has huge outliers that wreck the y-axis scaling. Thoughts?

sam (PM): thanks elaine, saw the screenshot. +1 on tick density, maybe reduce to 5 ticks and add adaptive labels. For units I'd prefer short: use 'ms' but ensure hover shows full 'milliseconds'.

maria (Eng): TBH the outliers are from a rare batch job — we could clip the plot area and show a toggle for "show full range". That keeps the main view useful. Also suggest offering log-scale option for the y-axis.

elaine (Design): Agree on clipping + toggle. UI copy idea: "Show full range (may include extreme outliers)" — does that read okay? Also thinking about accessibility: screen readers should announce axis units. Maybe ARIA on the chart svg?

maria (Eng): Yep, we can add an aria-label on the svg. Example:

```
<svg role="img" aria-label="Throughput over time, y axis in milliseconds, x axis time of day">...</svg>
```

That should make NVDA/JAWS read the units.

sam (PM): Nice. For tick density consider: desktop = 6 ticks, tablet = 4, mobile = 2. Also keep fractional avoidance — prefer rounded values (e.g., 0, 250, 500 ms) if data range allows.

elaine (Design): Good. Question about unit abbreviation style: lowercase 'ms' vs uppercase 'MS'? Recommend 'ms' per style guide. And let's add a tooltip on hover: full text "milliseconds".

maria (Eng): Leaning toward 'ms' too. Implementation note: if we abbreviate on axis labels, include a small legend element near the axis: "ms = milliseconds" — accessible via aria-describedby as well.

elaine (Design): UX nits: 1) when an outlier is clipped, show a subtle chevron at the top of the plot band with a tooltip like "X values clipped — click to expand" 2) smoothing toggle: default off, but show a faint dashed smoothed line when enabled. 3) color contrast: the thin gridlines are too low-contrast against the background per WCAG AA for 12pt text; bump to a stronger gray.

sam (PM): Agree on default smoothing off. For the chevron, maybe use a collapsed badge with an affordance: "+2 outliers hidden" — quick insight.

maria (Eng): Implementation detail: clipping vs aggregating — clipping is easiest but might mislead; we could compute a 95th percentile marker and offer both options: "clip to 95th percentile" or "show full range". Which copy would you prefer for the control?

elaine (Design): Options for copy: A) "Clip to 95th percentile (recommended)" B) "Show full range (may include extreme outliers)". I prefer A on the toggle default state and B as the secondary action. Thoughts?

sam (PM): A sounds good as default. Important we surface the chosen mode in the chart header so users know.

maria (Eng): One more accessibility thought: for keyboard users, toggles and the "show full range" action need focus styles and a keyboard shortcut (e.g., press 'O' to toggle outliers view when the chart has focus). I'll add that to the PR.

elaine (Design): Excellent. Last small copy: axis label suffixes — do we include unit in label ("Latency (ms)") or place unit only on axis ticks? My vote: include in label "Latency (ms)" for clarity, and keep tick labels numeric only (e.g., 0, 250, 500).

sam (PM): +1 for "Latency (ms)" as label. Also ensure export CSV includes units column header.

design-bot: Screenshot uploaded by elaine (Design): metrics-chart-v3.png :camera: (version 3)

elaine (Design): Cool, I'll update the mock with the 95th percentile control and chevron treatment and post a new PNG. Thanks for the quick feedback! :heart:

sam (PM): Thanks all — merging consensus and will add to spec for the next sprint.

maria (Eng): I'll stub the aria-label and keyboard shortcut in my branch and tag you for review @elaine.

elaine (Design): Perfect — leaving this thread. Follow-up in the next design pass if anything pops up.
